decisions.decision: The always-on `database` design gate does NOT fire for this change, and no grill-me pass was run.
decisions.why: The change is docs + spec only - zero migrations, zero schema objects, zero Go changes (tasks.md header and task 5.6 both assert it, and 5.6 gates on `git diff --stat` touching only .md). There is also no competing design to grill: the artifacts were authored and validated earlier, and RM7 already settled the underlying rule with the user across decisions RD1-RD12.

decisions.decision: Dispatch ONE worker identified as `platform` with explicitly granted paths, rather than a module-sandboxed worker or four per-module workers.
decisions.why: There is no `internal/platform` module - openspec/config.yaml designates `platform-` for cross-cutting changes. The file set spans two repo-root docs plus four modules' AGENTS.md, so no single Modules-Root child owns it. SKILL Step 0 allows a sandbox of 'one child of this folder PLUS explicitly granted paths'. Four per-module workers would each re-read the doc pack and, per task 4.5, are the drift risk the change exists to prevent; one coherent pass keeps the five copies consistent.

review.brief:
Review the DIFF of commit 2cc1902 (`git show 2cc1902`). Docs-and-spec only. Validate in priority order:
(1) TRUTHFULNESS OF THE NEW RULE - the point of the change. The old rule was FALSE after RM7; the new one must be TRUE. Check the rewritten text in CLAUDE.md and ai/go-conventions.md against the SHIPPED code on main: internal/tesla keeps native units (miles/bar) behind Km()/Kmh()/PSI() companions backed by milesToKm and barToPSI; internal/telemetry holds zero conversion; vehicle_snapshots stores km/C/PSI under suffixed names. Any clause that misdescribes the code is a BLOCKER - a doc that is wrong in a new way is worse than the stale one it replaced.
(2) The rule must be CHECKABLE, not vague: the concrete suffix list (_km, _kmh, _c, _psi, _kwh, _kw, _v, _a, _pct), both named exemptions (vendor adapter DTOs; monetary amounts paired with a currency column), and the NEGATIVE half (identifiers, timestamps, dates, counts, names, states, flags take NO suffix - so captured_at, tesla_id and max_range_charge_counter are not violations). A rule an agent cannot apply mechanically fails task 2.2.
(3) CLAUDE.md is loaded on EVERY request, so per task 3.2 it must carry the rule compressed and point at ai/go-conventions.md for the rationale. If the CLAUDE.md bullet is bloated or duplicates the long-form rationale, that is a finding - bloating it wastes the tokens the AI-efficiency non-negotiable exists to save. Also verify task 3.3: no contradiction with the Performance-Profile line it follows from.
(4) Task 4.5 - the four module AGENTS.md edits must be POINTERS plus that module's own fact, NOT five copies of one paragraph. Verify each carries a genuinely module-specific fact: telemetry (the table the rule was generalised from), manualcharge (compliant columns + price as the monetary exemption), account (no unit-bearing columns today, future-only), tesla (the named exception, sole owner of the conversion factors, with the warning against 'fixing' it to store km). Verify the AUDIT FACTS are true, not asserted - check the actual migrations.
(5) Task 4.6 is a prohibition: internal/battery/AGENTS.md and internal/gateway/AGENTS.md must NOT be edited. Confirm they are absent from the diff.
(6) RM7 tier 2 already rewrote internal/telemetry/AGENTS.md's DTO/units section. Confirm this change ADDED a pointer without clobbering that module-local content.
(7) Scope: no .go, .sql, sqlc.yaml or template file touched, and NOTHING under openspec/changes/archive/ or openspec/roadmaps/archive/ - those are immutable.
(8) ANTI-GAMING, verify independently: tasks 5.1 and 5.2 are recorded BLOCKED as obsolete (decision D3), and 5.4 was satisfied by a different method than its text says (decision D5). Do NOT take the leader's word for either. For 5.1/5.2, confirm telemetry-store-display-units really is archived and RD12 really was amended in-flight during RM7 - if the work was actually skippable-but-doable, that is a finding. For 5.4, the leader audited the resulting schema on a disposable container instead of grepping migrations, because migrations are append-only history and older statements legitimately name pre-rename columns; sanity-check that reasoning. No task title or criterion may have been edited or deleted.
This is a docs change: there is nothing to build or test. Do NOT run make migrate-*/db-* or psql - .env points at the user's real database. Never call the live Tesla API. Escalate on doubt: return changes-requested rather than approving anything you are unsure of.
